docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: CoBaIR is a python library for Context Based Intention Recognition. It provides the means to infer an intention from given context. An intention is a binary value e.g. repair pipe that can either be present or not. Only one intention can be present at a time. Context on the otherhand can have multiple discrete instantiations e.g. weather:sunny|cloudy|raining. If context values are continuous, discretizer functions can be used to create discrete values. From the inferred intention in a HRI scenario the robot can perform corresponding actions to help the human with a specific task.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
CoBaIR needs Python >= 3.10, the web GUI needs Python >= 3.11. Install it with the extras you need:

pip install "cobair[all]"
extra contains cobair the config model only (pyyaml) cobair[infer] inference with the Bayesian net (pgmpy, bnlearn), needed for cobair.bayes_net cobair[qt] the Qt configurator (PyQt5, pyqtgraph) cobair[web] the web GUI (Reflex, Python >= 3.11) cobair[all] everything above (Python >= 3.11, use cobair[infer,qt] on Python 3.10)

You can install the library from your local copy after cloning this repo with pip using pip install ".[all]" or install the newest unreleased features from the main branch with pip install "cobair[all] @ git+https://github.com/dfki-ric/CoBaIR.git@main"

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
from cobair.model import Config
from cobair.infer import Inference

config = Config.load('small_example.yml')
inference = Inference(config)
intention, decision_threshold, probabilities = inference.infer({'speech commands': 'pickup'})

cobair.model.Config holds the scenario and has methods to edit, validate, load and save it. cobair.infer.Inference infers the intentions for given evidence. See the API documentation.

The 4.x API (from CoBaIR.bayes_net import BayesNet, load_config) still works until 6.0.0, but raises a DeprecationWarning.

docs.title: Bayesian Approach
docs.text:
The configuration file for a two layer bayesian net for context based intention recognition follows the given format:

# List of contexts. Contexts can have different discrete instantiations.
# Number of instantiations must be larger than 1.
# For all discrete instantiations a prior probability must be given(sum for one context must be 1)
contexts:
  context 1:
    instantiation 1 : float
      .
    instantiation m_1 : float
  context n:
    instantiation 1 : float
      .
    instantiation m_n : float
# List of intentions. Intentions are always binary(either present or not)
# For every intention the context variables and their influence on the intention is given
# [very high, high, medium, low, very low, no] => [5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]
intentions:
  intention 1:
    context 1:
        instantiation 1: int # one out of [5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]
        .
        instantiation m_1: int # one out of [5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]
    context n:
        instantiation 1: int # one out of [5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]
        .
        instantiation m_n: int # one out of [5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]
  intention p:
    context 1:
        instantiation 1: int # one out of [5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]
        .
        instantiation m_1: int # one out of [5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]
    context n:
        instantiation 1: int # one out of [5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]
        .
        instantiation m_n: int # one out of [5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]
# decision_threshold is a float value between 0 and 1 which decides
# when an intention should be considered in inference.
# Probability must be greater than decision_threshold.
decision_threshold: float

docs.title: Run tests
docs.text:
Tests are implemented with pytest. All dependencies are declared in pyproject.toml; the development tools are dependency groups (test, docs, lint, e2e), which need pip >= 25.1. Install the test dependencies with

pip install --group test -e ".[all]"

Then you can run

python -m pytest tests/

You can as well see the test report for a specific commit in the Tests workflow runs (artifact test-reports-py<version>)

docs.title: Coverage

coverage run -m pytest tests/

coverage report

or

coverage html

docs.title: Code quality
docs.text:
The Quality workflow runs on every Pull Request into main and on pushes to main and counts ruff linting issues and the docstring coverage measured by interrogate. Both tools are configured in pyproject.toml and pinned in its lint dependency group. Run them locally with

pip install --group lint
ruff check .
interrogate -c pyproject.toml .

The workflow works as a ratchet against .github/quality-baseline.json: it fails if the number of ruff issues goes up or the docstring coverage goes down. If the numbers improved, lower ruff_issues / raise doc_coverage in the baseline in the same Pull Request to lock the improvement in. The badges at the top of this README are only committed by the workflow on main; on other branches and Pull Requests the numbers are shown in the job summary.

The test coverage badge comes from the coverage job of the Tests workflow. It combines the coverage of the cobair package from the Python 3.12 tests with all extras and from the end-to-end tests, including the cobair-web server they start (configured in [tool.coverage.*] of pyproject.toml). It is only shown, not enforced. Measure it locally with

pip install -e ".[all]"
coverage run -m pytest tests/ && coverage combine && coverage report

docs.title: API
docs.text:
CoBaIR is split into the config model and the inference:

  • cobair.model describes a scenario (contexts, intentions, influences, decision threshold), validates it, reads and writes config files and computes the conditional probability tables. It only needs pyyaml.
  • cobair.infer infers the intentions for given evidence with the two-layer Bayesian net. It needs the [infer] extra: pip install "cobair[infer]".
from cobair.model import Config
from cobair.infer import Inference

config = Config.load('small_example.yml')
config.change_influence_value('pick up tool', 'speech commands', 'pickup', 5)
print(config.validate())  # [] if the config is valid

inference = Inference(config)  # create a new Inference after editing the config
intention, decision_threshold, probabilities = inference.infer({'speech commands': 'pickup'})

docs.title: cobair.model
docs.text:
The config model of CoBaIR: contexts, intentions, influences and the decision threshold.

This module is pure Python (it only needs pyyaml), so it can be used without the inference dependencies, e.g. in the GUIs. The conditional probability tables of the two-layer Bayesian net are computed here as well, cobair.infer only hands them to pgmpy.

Example 
from cobair.model import Config

config = Config.load('small_example.yml')
config.add_context('weather', {'sunny': 0.7, 'rainy': 0.3})
config.change_influence_value('pick up tool', 'weather', 'rainy', 4)
print(config.validate())  # [] if the config is valid
config.save('my_config.yml')

docs.title: CPTs dataclass
docs.text:
The conditional probability tables of the two-layer Bayesian net.

The order of the states is the order of the instantiations in the config. The columns of the intention tables iterate over all combinations of context instantiations in the order of contexts, the last context changes fastest (the order pgmpy expects).

Attributes:

Name Type Description contexts list

All contexts, the parents of every intention.

states dict

The instantiations of every context.

context_priors dict

The apriori probability of every instantiation of every context.

intentions list

All intentions.

intention_values dict

For every intention [negative values, positive values].

Source code in cobair/model.py 
@dataclass
class CPTs:
    """The conditional probability tables of the two-layer Bayesian net.

    The order of the states is the order of the instantiations in the config.
    The columns of the intention tables iterate over all combinations of context instantiations
    in the order of `contexts`, the last context changes fastest (the order pgmpy expects).

    Attributes:
        contexts: All contexts, the parents of every intention.
        states: The instantiations of every context.
        context_priors: The apriori probability of every instantiation of every context.
        intentions: All intentions.
        intention_values: For every intention `[negative values, positive values]`.
    """

    contexts: list
    states: dict
    context_priors: dict
    intentions: list
    intention_values: dict

    @property
    def cards(self) -> list:
        """The number of instantiations of every context in the order of `contexts`.

        Returns:
            list: The cardinalities.
        """
        return [len(self.states[context]) for context in self.contexts]

class Config:
    """A mutable CoBaIR config.

    Attributes:
        contexts: `{context: {instantiation: apriori probability}}`
        intentions: `{intention: {context: {instantiation: influence}}}`. Combined influences use
            a tuple of contexts as context key and a tuple of instantiations as instantiation key.
        decision_threshold: The probability an intention must exceed to be picked.
    """

    def __init__(self, contexts: dict = None, intentions: dict = None,
                 decision_threshold: float = 0.0) -> None:
        """Create a config, the given dicts are copied.

        Args:
            contexts: `{context: {instantiation: apriori probability}}`
            intentions: `{intention: {context: {instantiation: influence}}}`
            decision_threshold: The probability an intention must exceed to be picked.
        """
        self.contexts = _to_plain(contexts or {})
        self.intentions = _to_plain(intentions or {})
        self.decision_threshold = decision_threshold

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # conversion and files

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, config: dict) -> Config:
        """Create a config from a dict in the config file format; unknown keys are ignored.

        Args:
            config: A dict with the keys `contexts`, `intentions` and `decision_threshold`.

        Returns:
            Config: The new config.
        """
        config = config or {}
        return cls(config.get('contexts'), config.get('intentions'),
                   config.get('decision_threshold', 0.0))

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        """Return the config as plain dicts in the config file format (without header).

        Returns:
            dict: A deep copy of the config.
        """
        return {'contexts': deepcopy(self.contexts),
                'intentions': deepcopy(self.intentions),
                'decision_threshold': self.decision_threshold}

    def copy(self) -> Config:
        """Return a deep copy.

        Returns:
            Config: The copy.
        """
        return Config.from_dict(self.to_dict())

    @classmethod
    def loads(cls, text: str) -> Config:
        """Create a config from YAML text.

        Args:
            text: The content of a config file.

        Returns:
            Config: The loaded config.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the text is not a mapping or was written with a newer format version.
        """
        data = yaml.load(text, Loader=PrettySafeLoader)  # noqa: S506 - safe loader + tuples
        if data is None:
            data = {}
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            raise ValueError('A config must be a YAML mapping')
        format_version = data.get('format_version', FORMAT_VERSION)
        if not isinstance(format_version, int) or format_version > FORMAT_VERSION:
            raise ValueError(
                f'The config has format version {format_version}, but cobair {__version__} '
                f'only supports up to version {FORMAT_VERSION}. Please update cobair.')
        return cls.from_dict(data)

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path) -> Config:
        """Load a config from a YAML file.

        Args:
            path: Path to the config file.

        Returns:
            Config: The loaded config.
        """
        return cls.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding='utf-8'))

    def dumps(self) -> str:
        """Return the config as YAML text with header.

        Returns:
            str: The content of a config file.
        """
        data = {'format_version': FORMAT_VERSION, 'created_with': f'cobair {__version__}'}
        data.update(self.to_dict())
        return HEADER + yaml.dump(data, Dumper=_Dumper, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True)

    def save(self, path) -> None:
        """Save the config to a YAML file.

        Args:
            path: Path to the config file.
        """
        Path(path).write_text(self.dumps(), encoding='utf-8')

    def __eq__(self, other) -> bool:
        """Configs are equal if contexts, intentions and decision threshold are equal.

        Args:
            other: The object to compare with.

        Returns:
            bool: True if equal.
        """
        if not isinstance(other, Config):
            return NotImplemented
        return self.to_dict() == other.to_dict()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # validation

    def validate(self) -> list:
        """Check that the config is complete and consistent.

        Returns:
            list: Messages describing all problems, empty if the config is valid.
        """
        problems = []
        if not self.contexts:
            problems.append('No contexts defined')
        if not self.intentions:
            problems.append('No intentions defined')
        if not _is_number(self.decision_threshold) or not 0 <= self.decision_threshold < 1:
            problems.append('Decision threshold must be a number between 0 and 1')

        for context, instantiations in self.contexts.items():
            for instantiation, value in instantiations.items():
                if not _is_number(value):
                    problems.append(
                        f'Apriori probability of context "{context}.{instantiation}" '
                        'is not a number')
            values = [value for value in instantiations.values() if _is_number(value)]
            if len(values) == len(instantiations) and \
                    not math.isclose(sum(values), 1.0, abs_tol=1e-9):
                problems.append(
                    'The sum of probabilities for context instantiations must be 1 - '
                    f'For "{context}" it is {sum(values)}!')

        for intention, influences in self.intentions.items():
            for context, values in influences.items():
                problems.extend(self._validate_influences(intention, context, values))
        return problems

    def _validate_influences(self, intention, context, values: dict) -> list:
        """Check the influence values of one intention for one (combined) context.

        Args:
            intention: The intention.
            context: A context or a tuple of contexts.
            values: `{instantiation: influence}`

        Returns:
            list: Messages describing all problems.
        """
        problems = []
        contexts = context if isinstance(context, tuple) else (context,)
        unknown = [name for name in contexts if name not in self.contexts]
        if unknown:
            return [f'Context influence {context} of {intention} cannot be found in the defined '
                    f'contexts! Unknown: {unknown}']
        for instantiation, influence in values.items():
            if isinstance(context, tuple):
                if not isinstance(instantiation, tuple) or len(instantiation) != len(context) \
                        or any(inst not in self.contexts[name]
                               for name, inst in zip(context, instantiation)):
                    problems.append(f'{instantiation} is not a valid combination of '
                                    f'instantiations for {context} in {intention}')
            elif instantiation not in self.contexts[context]:
                problems.append(
                    'An influence needs to be defined for all instantiations! '
                    f'{intention}.{context}.{instantiation} does not fit the defined '
                    f'instantiations for {context}')
            if not (isinstance(influence, int) and not isinstance(influence, bool)
                    and 0 <= influence <= 5):
                problems.append(f'Influence Value for {intention}.{context}.{instantiation} '
                                f'must be an integer between 0 and 5! Is {influence}')
        return problems

    @property
    def valid(self) -> bool:
        """True if `validate()` finds no problems.

        Returns:
            bool: Validity of the config.
        """
        return not self.validate()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # editing

    def add_context(self, context: Hashable, instantiations: dict) -> None:
        """Add a new context; its influence on all intentions is set to 0.

        Args:
            context: Name of the new context.
            instantiations: `{instantiation: apriori probability}`, e.g. `{True: 0.6, False: 0.4}`

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the context already exists.
        """
        if context in self.contexts:
            raise ValueError(
                'Cannot add existing context - use edit_context to edit an existing context')
        self.contexts[context] = dict(instantiations)
        self._sync_influences()

    def edit_context(self, context: Hashable, instantiations: dict,
                     new_name: Hashable = None) -> None:
        """Change the instantiations of a context and optionally rename it.

        Influences of removed instantiations are removed, new instantiations get the influence 0.
        Combined influences follow a rename and are removed if they use a removed instantiation.

        !!! note
            Changing the name of an instantiation will always set the influence value of this
                instantiation to zero for all intentions!

        Args:
            context: Name of the context to edit.
            instantiations: `{instantiation: apriori probability}`, e.g. `{True: 0.6, False: 0.4}`
            new_name: A new name for the context.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the context does not exist or `new_name` is another existing context.
        """
        if context not in self.contexts:
            raise ValueError(
                'Cannot edit non existing context - use add_context to add a new context')
        if new_name is not None and new_name != context:
            if new_name in self.contexts:
                raise ValueError(f'Cannot rename "{context}" to "{new_name}" - it exists already')
            self.contexts = _rename_key(self.contexts, context, new_name)
            for intention, influences in self.intentions.items():
                renamed = {}
                for key, values in influences.items():
                    if key == context:
                        renamed[new_name] = values
                    elif isinstance(key, tuple) and context in key:
                        renamed[tuple(new_name if name == context else name for name in key)] = \
                            values
                    else:
                        renamed[key] = values
                self.intentions[intention] = renamed
            context = new_name
        self.contexts[context] = dict(instantiations)
        self._sync_influences()

    def del_context(self, context: Hashable) -> None:
        """Remove a context including all its (combined) influences.

        Args:
            context: Name of the context to delete.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the context does not exist.
        """
        if context not in self.contexts:
            raise ValueError(
                'Cannot delete non-existing context - use add_context to add a new context')
        del self.contexts[context]
        self._sync_influences()

    def add_intention(self, intention: Hashable) -> None:
        """Add a new intention; the influence of all contexts is set to 0.

        Args:
            intention: Name of the new intention.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the intention already exists.
        """
        if intention in self.intentions:
            raise ValueError(
                'Cannot add existing intention - use edit_intention to edit an existing intention')
        self.intentions[intention] = {}
        self._sync_influences()

    def edit_intention(self, intention: Hashable, new_name: Hashable) -> None:
        """Rename an intention.

        Args:
            intention: Name of the intention to edit.
            new_name: A new name for the intention.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the intention does not exist or `new_name` exists already.
        """
        if intention not in self.intentions:
            raise ValueError(
                'Cannot edit non existing intention - use add_intention to add a new intention')
        if new_name in self.intentions:
            raise ValueError(f'{new_name} exists - cannot be given as the new name for {intention}')
        self.intentions = _rename_key(self.intentions, intention, new_name)

    def del_intention(self, intention: Hashable) -> None:
        """Remove an intention.

        Args:
            intention: Name of the intention to delete.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the intention does not exist.
        """
        if intention not in self.intentions:
            raise ValueError(
                'Cannot delete non existing intention - use add_intention to add a new intention')
        del self.intentions[intention]

    def change_context_apriori_value(self, context: Hashable, instantiation: Hashable,
                                     value: float) -> None:
        """Change the apriori probability of a context instantiation.

        Args:
            context: Name of the context.
            instantiation: The instantiation.
            value: The new apriori probability.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the context or instantiation does not exist.
        """
        if instantiation not in self.contexts.get(context, {}):
            raise ValueError(
                'change_context_apriori_value can only change values that exist already')
        self.contexts[context][instantiation] = value

    def change_influence_value(self, intention: Hashable, context: Hashable,
                               instantiation: Hashable, value: int) -> None:
        """Change the influence of a context instantiation on an intention.

        Args:
            intention: Name of the intention.
            context: Name of the context (or tuple of contexts for a combined influence).
            instantiation: The instantiation (or tuple of instantiations).
            value: The new influence value, one out of [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5].

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the influence does not exist.
        """
        if instantiation not in self.intentions.get(intention, {}).get(context, {}):
            raise ValueError('change_influence_value can only change values that exist already')
        self.intentions[intention][context][instantiation] = value

    def add_combined_influence(self, intention: Hashable, contexts: tuple,
                               instantiations: tuple, value: int) -> None:
        """Set the influence of a combination of context instantiations on an intention.

        If all instantiations of the combination are present, the combined influence replaces
        the single influences of these contexts.

        Args:
            intention: Name of the intention.
            contexts: The names of the contexts.
            instantiations: One instantiation for each of the contexts.
            value: The influence value, one out of [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5].

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the contexts are empty, the intention does not exist or an
                instantiation does not exist.
        """
        if not contexts:
            raise ValueError('Contexts list cannot be empty.')
        if intention not in self.intentions:
            raise ValueError(f'"{intention}" does not exist in the list of intentions')
        contexts, instantiations = tuple(contexts), tuple(instantiations)
        if len(contexts) != len(instantiations) or any(
                instantiation not in self.contexts.get(context, {})
                for context, instantiation in zip(contexts, instantiations)):
            raise ValueError(
                'add_combined_influence can only combine context instantiations that already exist')
        self.intentions[intention].setdefault(contexts, {})[instantiations] = value

    def del_combined_influence(self, intention: Hashable, contexts: tuple,
                               instantiations: tuple) -> None:
        """Remove the combined influence of a combination of context instantiations.

        Args:
            intention: Name of the intention.
            contexts: The names of the contexts.
            instantiations: One instantiation for each of the contexts.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the combined influence does not exist.
        """
        contexts, instantiations = tuple(contexts), tuple(instantiations)
        combinations = self.intentions.get(intention, {}).get(contexts, {})
        if instantiations not in combinations:
            raise ValueError('Combined context instantiations must exist to be removed.')
        del combinations[instantiations]
        if not combinations:
            del self.intentions[intention][contexts]

    def change_decision_threshold(self, decision_threshold: float) -> None:
        """Change the decision threshold.

        Args:
            decision_threshold: The new decision threshold.
        """
        self.decision_threshold = decision_threshold

    def combined_influences(self, intention: Hashable) -> dict:
        """Return the combined influences of an intention.

        Args:
            intention: Name of the intention.

        Returns:
            dict: `{(context, ...): {(instantiation, ...): influence}}`
        """
        return {contexts: values for contexts, values in self.intentions[intention].items()
                if isinstance(contexts, tuple)}

    def _sync_influences(self) -> None:
        """Make the influences of all intentions match the contexts and their instantiations."""
        for intention, influences in self.intentions.items():
            synced = {}
            for context, instantiations in self.contexts.items():
                old = influences.get(context, {})
                synced[context] = {instantiation: old.get(instantiation, 0)
                                   for instantiation in instantiations}
            for contexts, combinations in influences.items():
                if not isinstance(contexts, tuple) or \
                        any(context not in self.contexts for context in contexts):
                    continue
                kept = {instantiations: value for instantiations, value in combinations.items()
                        if all(instantiation in self.contexts[context]
                               for context, instantiation in zip(contexts, instantiations))}
                if kept:
                    synced[contexts] = kept
            self.intentions[intention] = synced

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # conditional probability tables

    def cpts(self) -> CPTs:
        """Compute the conditional probability tables of the two-layer Bayesian net.

        The probability of an intention for a combination of context instantiations is the
        average of the probabilities of the influences (see `INFLUENCE_TO_PROBABILITY`).
        If a combined influence matches the combination, its value replaces the single influences
        of the combined contexts; if several match, the first one wins.

        Returns:
            CPTs: The conditional probability tables.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the config is not valid.
        """
        problems = self.validate()
        if problems:
            raise ValueError(f'Invalid configuration: {problems}')
        contexts = list(self.contexts)
        states = {context: list(instantiations) for context, instantiations in
                  self.contexts.items()}
        priors = {context: list(instantiations.values()) for context, instantiations in
                  self.contexts.items()}
        values = {intention: self._intention_values(contexts, states, influences)
                  for intention, influences in self.intentions.items()}
        return CPTs(contexts, states, priors, list(self.intentions), values)

    @staticmethod
    def _intention_values(contexts: list, states: dict, influences: dict) -> list:
        """Compute the CPT of one intention.

        Args:
            contexts: All contexts in CPT order.
            states: The instantiations of every context.
            influences: `{context: {instantiation: influence}}` of the intention.

        Returns:
            list: `[negative values, positive values]`
        """
        combined = [(names, combination, value)
                    for names, combinations in influences.items() if isinstance(names, tuple)
                    for combination, value in combinations.items()]
        positive = []
        for case in itertools.product(*(states[context] for context in contexts)):
            active = dict(zip(contexts, case))
            # missing influences count as 0
            case_influences = {context: influences.get(context, {}).get(active[context], 0)
                               for context in contexts}
            for names, combination, value in combined:
                if all(active[name] == instantiation
                       for name, instantiation in zip(names, combination)):
                    case_influences.update(dict.fromkeys(names, value))
                    break
            probabilities = [INFLUENCE_TO_PROBABILITY.get(influence, 0)
                             for influence in case_influences.values()]
            positive.append(sum(probabilities) / len(probabilities) if probabilities else 0)
        return [[1 - value for value in positive], positive]

def add_combined_influence(self, intention: Hashable, contexts: tuple,
                           instantiations: tuple, value: int) -> None:
    """Set the influence of a combination of context instantiations on an intention.

    If all instantiations of the combination are present, the combined influence replaces
    the single influences of these contexts.

    Args:
        intention: Name of the intention.
        contexts: The names of the contexts.
        instantiations: One instantiation for each of the contexts.
        value: The influence value, one out of [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5].

    Raises:

            instantiation does not exist.

    if not contexts:
        raise ValueError('Contexts list cannot be empty.')
    if intention not in self.intentions:
        raise ValueError(f'"{intention}" does not exist in the list of intentions')
    contexts, instantiations = tuple(contexts), tuple(instantiations)
    if len(contexts) != len(instantiations) or any(
            instantiation not in self.contexts.get(context, {})
            for context, instantiation in zip(contexts, instantiations)):

    self.intentions[intention].setdefault(contexts, {})[instantiations] = value

def edit_context(self, context: Hashable, instantiations: dict,
                 new_name: Hashable = None) -> None:
    """Change the instantiations of a context and optionally rename it.

    Influences of removed instantiations are removed, new instantiations get the influence 0.
    Combined influences follow a rename and are removed if they use a removed instantiation.

    !!! note
        Changing the name of an instantiation will always set the influence value of this
            instantiation to zero for all intentions!

    Args:
        context: Name of the context to edit.
        instantiations: `{instantiation: apriori probability}`, e.g. `{True: 0.6, False: 0.4}`
        new_name: A new name for the context.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the context does not exist or `new_name` is another existing context.
    """
    if context not in self.contexts:
        raise ValueError(
            'Cannot edit non existing context - use add_context to add a new context')
    if new_name is not None and new_name != context:
        if new_name in self.contexts:
            raise ValueError(f'Cannot rename "{context}" to "{new_name}" - it exists already')
        self.contexts = _rename_key(self.contexts, context, new_name)
        for intention, influences in self.intentions.items():
            renamed = {}
            for key, values in influences.items():
                if key == context:
                    renamed[new_name] = values
                elif isinstance(key, tuple) and context in key:
                    renamed[tuple(new_name if name == context else name for name in key)] = \
                        values
                else:
                    renamed[key] = values
            self.intentions[intention] = renamed
        context = new_name
    self.contexts[context] = dict(instantiations)
    self._sync_influences()

def loads(cls, text: str) -> Config:
    """Create a config from YAML text.

        raise ValueError(
            f'The config has format version {format_version}, but cobair {__version__} '
            f'only supports up to version {FORMAT_VERSION}. Please update cobair.')
    return cls.from_dict(data)

def validate(self) -> list:
    """Check that the config is complete and consistent.

    Returns:
        list: Messages describing all problems, empty if the config is valid.
    """
    problems = []
    if not self.contexts:
        problems.append('No contexts defined')
    if not self.intentions:
        problems.append('No intentions defined')
    if not _is_number(self.decision_threshold) or not 0 <= self.decision_threshold < 1:
        problems.append('Decision threshold must be a number between 0 and 1')

    for context, instantiations in self.contexts.items():
        for instantiation, value in instantiations.items():
            if not _is_number(value):
                problems.append(
                    f'Apriori probability of context "{context}.{instantiation}" '
                    'is not a number')
        values = [value for value in instantiations.values() if _is_number(value)]
        if len(values) == len(instantiations) and \
                not math.isclose(sum(values), 1.0, abs_tol=1e-9):
            problems.append(
                'The sum of probabilities for context instantiations must be 1 - '
                f'For "{context}" it is {sum(values)}!')

    for intention, influences in self.intentions.items():
        for context, values in influences.items():
            problems.extend(self._validate_influences(intention, context, values))
    return problems

class Inference:
    """Infers the probabilities of the intentions of a valid config.

    The inference works on a copy of the config: create a new `Inference` after editing it.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: Config) -> None:
        """Build the Bayesian net for a config, which must be valid (else `ValueError`).

        Args:
            config: A valid config.
        """
        self.config = config.copy()
        self.cpts = self.config.cpts()
        self.discretization_functions = {}
        # bnlearn uses the index of an instantiation (card) instead of the instantiation
        self.value_to_card = {context: {value: card for card, value in enumerate(states)}
                              for context, states in self.cpts.states.items()}
        self.tabular_cpds = self._create_tabular_cpds()
        edges = list(itertools.product(self.cpts.contexts, self.cpts.intentions))
        self.dag = bn.make_DAG(edges, CPD=self.tabular_cpds)

    def _create_tabular_cpds(self) -> list:
        """Wrap the CPTs in pgmpy TabularCPDs.

        Returns:
            list: One TabularCPD per context and intention.
        """
        cpds = [TabularCPD(variable=context, variable_card=len(priors),
                           values=[[prior] for prior in priors])
                for context, priors in self.cpts.context_priors.items()]
        cpds += [TabularCPD(variable=intention,
                            variable_card=2,  # intentions are always binary
                            values=values,
                            evidence=self.cpts.contexts,
                            evidence_card=self.cpts.cards)
                 for intention, values in self.cpts.intention_values.items()]
        return cpds

    def bind_discretization_function(self, context: Hashable,
                                     discretization_function: Callable) -> None:
        """Bind a discretization function to a context.

        Args:
            context: One of the contexts of the config.
            discretization_function: A function which takes one parameter and returns one of the
                instantiations of the context.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the context does not exist.
        """
        if context not in self.config.contexts:
            raise ValueError(
                f'Cannot bind discretization function to {context}. Context does not exist!')
        self.discretization_functions[context] = discretization_function

    def check_evidence(self, context: Hashable, instantiation) -> tuple[bool, str]:
        """Check if an instantiation is valid evidence for a context.

        Args:
            context: A context.
            instantiation: An instantiation of the context.

        Returns:
            tuple[bool, str]: Validity and an error or warning message (empty if fine).
        """
        if context not in self.config.contexts:
            return True, f'Context "{context}" not set in config - will be ignored'
        if not isinstance(instantiation, Hashable):
            return False, ('Context instatiations must be hashable! '
                           f'Instantiation "{instantiation}" for context "{context}" '
                           'is not hashable!')
        if instantiation is None:
            return True, (f'No instantiation given for context "{context}" - '
                          'A prori values will be used.')
        if instantiation not in self.config.contexts[context]:
            return True, (f'"{instantiation}" is not a valid instantiation for "{context}". '
                          f'Using None instead Valid options are '
                          f'{list(self.config.contexts[context])}')
        return True, ''

    def _card_evidence(self, evidence: dict) -> dict:
        """Translate evidence into bnlearn's card form.

        Discretization functions are applied to values that are not an instantiation.

        Args:
            evidence: `{context: instantiation}`

        Returns:
            dict: `{context: card}` of all usable evidence.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If evidence is invalid.
        """
        card_evidence = {}
        errors = []
        for context, instantiation in evidence.items():
            if context in self.discretization_functions and instantiation is not None and \
                    not (isinstance(instantiation, Hashable)
                         and instantiation in self.value_to_card[context]):
                instantiation = self.discretization_functions[context](instantiation)
            valid, message = self.check_evidence(context, instantiation)
            if not valid:
                errors.append(message)
            elif message:
                warnings.warn(message, stacklevel=3)
            else:
                card_evidence[context] = self.value_to_card[context][instantiation]
        if errors:
            raise ValueError(f'{errors}')
        return card_evidence

    def infer(self, evidence: dict, normalized: bool = True,
              decision_threshold: float = None) -> InferenceResult:
        """Infer the probabilities of the intentions given evidence.

        Args:
            evidence: `{context: instantiation}`, e.g. `{'speech commands': 'pickup'}`.
                Contexts which are not in the config are ignored (with a warning),
                contexts which are not given use their apriori probabilities.
            normalized: Normalize the probabilities to sum up to 1.
            decision_threshold: A threshold for picking the most likely intention, between 0
                and 1. Defaults to the decision threshold of the config.

        Returns:
            InferenceResult: The most likely intention (None if the decision threshold is not
                exceeded), the decision threshold and the probabilities of all intentions.
        """
        if decision_threshold is None:
            decision_threshold = self.config.decision_threshold
        card_evidence = self._card_evidence(evidence)
        # only the probability of the True state of the binary intentions is kept
        probabilities = {
            intention: bn.inference.fit(self.dag, variables=[intention],
                                        evidence=card_evidence).values[1]
            for intention in self.cpts.intentions}
        if normalized:
            probabilities = normalize(probabilities)
        best = max(probabilities, key=probabilities.get)
        if probabilities[best] <= decision_threshold:
            best = None
        return InferenceResult(best, decision_threshold, probabilities)

def normalize(probabilities: dict) -> dict:
    """Normalize the probabilities of the intentions to a probability distribution.

    Each intention is inferred independently as True or False, so the raw probabilities don't sum
    up to 1 and can't be compared as a distribution over intentions.

    Args:
        probabilities: `{intention: probability}`

    Returns:
        dict: `{intention: normalized probability}`
    """
    total = sum(probabilities.values())
    return {intention: probability / total for intention, probability in probabilities.items()}

class BayesNet:
    """Deprecated facade over `cobair.model.Config` and `cobair.infer.Inference`.

    `config` is the source of truth like in 4.x: every method reads it, applies the change through
    `Config` and replaces it with the result.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: dict = None, bn_verbosity: int = 0, validate: bool = True) -> None:
        """Initializes the BayesNet with the given config.

        Args:
            config: A dict with a config following the config format.
            bn_verbosity: Ignored since bnlearn 1.x, which logs through `logging`.
            validate: Flag if the given config should be validated or not.
                This is necessary to load invalid configs
        """
        _deprecated('cobair.bayes_net.BayesNet', 'cobair.model.Config and cobair.infer.Inference')
        self.log = logging.getLogger(self.__class__.__name__)
        self.bn_verbosity = bn_verbosity
        self.discretization_functions = {}
        self.value_to_prob = INFLUENCE_TO_PROBABILITY
        self._set_config(Config.from_dict(config), validate=validate and config is not None)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # state

    def _model(self) -> Config:
        """Return the current `config` as `Config`.

        Returns:
            Config: The model.
        """
        return Config.from_dict(self.config)

    def _set_config(self, model: Config, validate: bool = True) -> None:
        """Replace the config and rebuild everything that depends on it, like `__init__` in 4.x.

        Args:
            model: The new config.
            validate: Flag if the config should be validated (with warnings).
        """
        self.config = _config_to_default_dict(model.to_dict())
        self.decision_threshold = model.decision_threshold
        self.contexts = self.evidence = list(model.contexts)
        self.intentions = list(model.intentions)
        self.edges = [(context, intention) for context in self.contexts
                      for intention in self.intentions]
        self.evidence_card = [len(model.contexts[context]) for context in self.contexts]
        self.value_to_card = defaultdict(dict, {
            context: {value: card for card, value in enumerate(instantiations)}
            for context, instantiations in model.contexts.items()})
        self.card_to_value = defaultdict(dict, {
            context: dict(enumerate(instantiations))
            for context, instantiations in model.contexts.items()})
        self.valid = self._validate(model) if validate else False
        self.inference = None
        self.cpts = self.DAG = None
        if self.valid:
            self.valid_config = _config_to_default_dict(model.to_dict())
            self.inference = Inference(model)
            self.inference.discretization_functions = self.discretization_functions
            self.cpts = self.inference.tabular_cpds
            self.DAG = self.inference.dag

    def _apply(self, method: str, *args) -> None:
        """Apply an editing method of `Config` and rebuild.

        Args:
            method: Name of the `Config` method.
            *args: Arguments of the method.
        """
        model = self._model()
        getattr(model, method)(*args)
        self._set_config(model)

    @staticmethod
    def _validate(model: Config) -> bool:
        """Validate with a warning for every problem.

        Args:
            model: The config.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the config is valid.
        """
        problems = model.validate()
        for problem in problems:
            warnings.warn(problem, stacklevel=4)
        return not problems

    def validate_config(self) -> bool:
        """Validate that the current config follows the correct format.

        Returns:
            bool: True if config is valid, False otherwise. A warning is raised for every problem.
        """
        model = self._model()
        self.valid = self._validate(model)
        if self.valid:
            self.valid_config = _config_to_default_dict(model.to_dict())
        return self.valid

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # editing

    def add_context(self, context: str, instantiations: dict):
        """This will add a new context to the config and updates the bayesNet.

        Args:
            context: a new context for the config
            instantiations: a dict of the instantiations and their apriori probabilities
        """
        self._apply('add_context', context, instantiations)

    def add_intention(self, intention: str):
        """This will add a new intention to the config and updates the bayesNet.

        Args:
            intention: Name of a new intention
        """
        self._apply('add_intention', intention)

    def edit_context(self, context: str, instantiations: dict, new_name: str = None):
        """Edits an existing context - this can also be used to remove instantiations.

        Args:
            context: Name of the context to edit
            instantiations: A Dict of instantiations and their apriori probabilities.
            new_name: A new name for the context
        """
        self._apply('edit_context', context, instantiations, new_name)

    def edit_intention(self, intention: str, new_name: str):
        """Edits an existing intention.

        Args:
            intention: Name of the intention to edit
            new_name: A new name for the intention
        """
        self._apply('edit_intention', intention, new_name)

    def del_context(self, context: str):
        """Removes a context.

        Args:
            context: Name of the context to delete
        """
        self._apply('del_context', context)

    def del_intention(self, intention):
        """Remove an intention.

        Args:
            intention: Name of the intention to delete
        """
        self._apply('del_intention', intention)

    def change_context_apriori_value(self, context: str, instantiation, value: float):
        """Changes the apriori_value for a context instantiation.

        Args:
            context: Name of the context
            instantiation: The instantiation for which the apriori value needs to be changed
            value: the new apriori value
        """
        self._apply('change_context_apriori_value', context, instantiation, value)

    def change_influence_value(self, intention: str, context: str, instantiation, value: int):
        """Update the influence value of a specific intention for a particular context instance.

        Args:
            intention: Name of the intention
            context: name of the context
            instantiation: The instantiation for which the influence value should be changed
            value: the new influence value. Can be one out of [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
        """
        self._apply('change_influence_value', intention, context, instantiation, value)

    def add_combined_influence(self, intention: str, contexts: tuple,
                               instantiations: tuple, value: int):
        """Adds an influence value for a combination of context instantiations.

        Args:
            intention: Name of the intention
            contexts: tuple containing the names of the contexts
            instantiations: Tuple of context instances to set influence value for.
            value: influence value. Can be one out of [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
        """
        self._apply('add_combined_influence', intention, contexts, instantiations, value)

    def del_combined_influence(self, intention: str, contexts: tuple, instantiations: tuple):
        """Removes the influence value for a combination of context instantiations.

        Args:
            intention: Name of the intention
            contexts: tuple containing the names of the contexts
            instantiations: tuple of context instantiations
        """
        self._apply('del_combined_influence', intention, contexts, instantiations)

    def change_decision_threshold(self, decision_threshold):
        """Changes the decision threshold in the config.

        Args:
            decision_threshold: The new decision threshold.
        """
        self._apply('change_decision_threshold', decision_threshold)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # files

    def save(self, path: str, save_invalid: bool = True):
        """Saves the config of the bayesNet to a yml file.

        Args:
            path: path to the file the config will be saved in
            save_invalid: Flag to decide if invalid configs can be saved
        """
        if not self.valid and not save_invalid:
            warnings.warn("Invalid configuration will not be saved.", stacklevel=2)
        else:
            self._model().save(path)

    def load(self, path: str):
        """Loads a config from file and reinitializes the bayesNet.

        Args:
            path: path to the file the config is saved in
        """
        self._set_config(Config.load(path))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # inference

    def bind_discretization_function(self, context, discretization_function):
        """Binds a discretization_function to a specific context.

        Args:
            context: One of the possible contexts from the config
            discretization_function: A discretization function which has to take one parameter
                and return one of the possible discrete context instantiations.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the context does not exist.
        """
        if context not in self.contexts:
            raise ValueError(
                f'Cannot bind discretization function to {context}. Context does not exist!')
        self.discretization_functions[context] = discretization_function

    def valid_evidence(self, context: str, instantiation) -> tuple[bool, str]:
        """Tests if evidence is a valid instantiation for the context.

        Args:
            context: a context
            instantiation: an instantiation of the context

        Returns:
            tuple[bool, str]: validity and an error/warn message

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the config is invalid.
        """
        if self.inference is None:
            raise ValueError('Invalid configuration')
        return self.inference.check_evidence(context, instantiation)

    def infer(self, evidence, normalized=True, decision_threshold=None) -> tuple:
        """Infers the probabilities for the intentions with given evidence.

        Args:
            evidence: Evidence to infer the probabilities of all intentions.
            normalized: Flag if the returned inference is normalized to sum up to 1.
            decision_threshold: a threshold for picking the most likely intention.

        Returns:
            tuple: the highest ranking intention (or None), the decision threshold and a
                dictionary of intentions and the corresponding probabilities.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the config is invalid.
        """
        if not self.valid or self.inference is None:
            raise ValueError('Invalid configuration')
        return self.inference.infer(evidence, normalized, decision_threshold)

    def normalize_inference(self, inference: dict) -> dict:
        """Normalizes the inference to a proper probability distribution.

        Args:
            inference: dictionary of intentions and the corresponding probabilities

        Returns:
            dict: dictionary of intentions and the corresponding normalized probabilities.
        """
        return normalize(inference)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # internals used by old tests

    def _calculate_probability_values(self, context_influence: dict) -> list:
        """Calculates the probability values with the given context_influence from the config.

        Args:
            context_influence: A dict with the influence values for contexts.

        Returns:
            list: `[negative values, positive values]`
        """
        states = {context: list(instantiations)
                  for context, instantiations in self.config['contexts'].items()}
        # pylint: disable-next=protected-access
        return Config._intention_values(self.evidence, states, context_influence)

    def _create_combined_context(self, context_influence: dict) -> dict:
        """Creates a dict with the combined contexts in card index format from context_influence.

        Args:
            context_influence: A dict with the influence values for contexts.

        Returns:
            dict: `{(context index, ...): {(instantiation, ...): influence}}`
        """
        return {tuple(map(self.evidence.index, context)): values
                for context, values in context_influence.items() if isinstance(context, tuple)}

docs.title: Migrating from 4.x to 5.0
docs.text: CoBaIR 5.0 splits the library into a config model and the inference, brings the web GUI and renames the package to lowercase cobair. Code written for 4.x keeps working in 5.x, it only shows DeprecationWarnings. The deprecated names are removed in 6.0.0 (#199).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
5.0 needs Python ≥ 3.10. The dependencies are split into extras:

4.x 5.0 pip install CoBaIR pip install "cobair[infer]" for the inference, "cobair[all]" for everything python start_configurator.py pip install "cobair[qt]", then cobair-qt new: pip install "cobair[web]", then cobair-web (Python ≥ 3.11)

pip install cobair alone installs only the config model (cobair.model, needs only pyyaml).

docs.title: Imports and API
docs.text:
4.x (deprecated) 5.0 import CoBaIR import cobair from CoBaIR.bayes_net import BayesNet from cobair.model import Config and from cobair.infer import Inference load_config(path) Config.load(path) BayesNet(config) config = Config.from_dict(config), inference = Inference(config) bayes_net.add_context(...), edit_context, del_context, add_intention, edit_intention, del_intention, change_context_apriori_value, change_influence_value, add_combined_influence, del_combined_influence, change_decision_threshold the same methods on Config bayes_net.validate_config() (warnings) config.validate() returns the problems as list, config.valid bayes_net.save(path) config.save(path) bayes_net.infer(evidence) Inference(config).infer(evidence) bayes_net.bind_discretization_function(...) inference.bind_discretization_function(...) from CoBaIR.configurator import Configurator from cobair.qt import Configurator

Example:

# 4.x
from CoBaIR.bayes_net import BayesNet, load_config
net = BayesNet(load_config('my_scenario.yml'))
intention, threshold, probabilities = net.infer({'speech commands': 'pickup'})

# 5.0
from cobair.model import Config
from cobair.infer import Inference
inference = Inference(Config.load('my_scenario.yml'))
intention, threshold, probabilities = inference.infer({'speech commands': 'pickup'})

Inference.infer returns a named tuple (intention, decision_threshold, probabilities), so the 4.x unpacking works unchanged. An Inference works on a copy of the config: create a new one after editing the config.

docs.title: Config files
docs.text: The YAML format is compatible in both directions: 5.0 reads 4.x files, and 4.x reads files written by 5.0. Files written by 5.0 start with a comment and the keys format_version and created_with, which 4.x ignores. Contexts, instantiations and intentions keep their order instead of being sorted alphabetically.

docs.title: Changed behaviour
docs.text:
These were bugs in 4.x. If your code relied on them, check the results:

  • Editing or deleting a context no longer deletes all combined influences. Renaming a context renames it in the combined influences.
  • All combinations of a context tuple count in the inference, 4.x only used the first one. del_combined_influence removes only the given combination.
  • Discretization functions run for every evidence value that is not an instantiation. In 4.x they only ran for unhashable values, so e.g. a float for a bool context was ignored with a warning.
  • Renaming a context to the name of another context raises a ValueError instead of overwriting it.
  • Apriori probabilities are checked to sum up to 1 with a small tolerance, so 0.1 + 0.2 + 0.7 is valid. Integers (e.g. a decision threshold of 0) count as numbers.

docs.title: Purpose of CoBaIR
docs.text: The CoBaIR framework is designed to interpret human intentions within diverse settings, assigning probabilities to these intentions based on the contextual information provided in multimodal scenarios.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Before starting to design a scenario with CoBaIR you need to understand some basics.

docs.title: Intentions
docs.text: Intentions denote what a human in an HRI scenario wants to do in a certain situation. An intention is a binary value e.g. repair pipe that can either be present or not. Only one intention can be present at a time.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Every perceivable aspect of the scenario is considered to be context in CoBaIR. Context can have multiple discrete instantiations e.g. weather:sunny|cloudy|raining. If context values are continuous, discretizer functions can be used to create discrete values.

docs.title: Configuring a CoBaIR Scenario with the GUI
docs.text: The screenshots show the web GUI (cobair-web). The Qt configurator (cobair-qt) has the same settings in a different layout.

docs.title: Apriori Probabilities
docs.text:
Apriori probabilities describe how likely each instantiation of a context is before anything is observed. They are used during inference whenever a context is not observed: CoBaIR then assumes that the instantiations occur with these probabilities. Once a context is observed, its apriori probabilities don't matter any more.

The apriori probabilities of a context must sum up to 1. If you don't know how often the instantiations occur, distribute the probability equally, e.g. 0.5 / 0.5 for two instantiations.

docs.title: Setting Apriori Probabilities
docs.text:
• Add a context with Add next to Contexts, or edit one with its pencil icon. The dialog sets the name of the context and its instantiations with their apriori probabilities.
  • The apriori probabilities can also be changed directly in the context cards.
  • If the probabilities of a context don't sum up to 1, the problems box above says so.

docs.title: Influence Values
docs.text:
An influence value describes how strongly an instantiation of a context indicates an intention. The scale goes from 0 to 5, each value stands for the probability of the intention given only this instantiation:

value meaning probability 0 not probable 0 % 1 not very probable 5 % 2 somewhat probable 25 % 3 even probability 50 % 4 very probable 75 % 5 definitely probable 95 %

For a combination of instantiations, CoBaIR averages these probabilities over all contexts. So every context contributes equally, and a single context can't decide an intention on its own. For this, use a combined context influence.

Ask yourself for every instantiation and intention: "If I only knew this, how probable would the intention be?"

docs.title: Setting Influence Values
docs.text: In the Influences section, choose a context. The table shows its instantiations as rows and the intentions as columns; choose a value of the scale in every cell. New contexts and intentions start with 0.

docs.title: Decision Threshold
docs.text: The decision threshold is the probability the most likely intention must exceed to be recognized. The inference always computes a probability for every intention (normalized, so they sum up to 1). If even the most likely intention doesn't exceed the threshold, no intention is recognized, which means "I am not sure".

docs.title: Importance of Setting It
docs.text: A robot that acts on an intention should be confident enough: a wrong action is often worse than waiting for more context. A high threshold (e.g. 0.8) makes the system cautious, a low one (e.g. 0.3) makes it react to weak evidence. With many intentions the probabilities are spread over more options, so the threshold usually needs to be lower than with two intentions.

docs.title: How to Set
docs.text: Enter a number between 0 and 1 in Decision threshold. Try the example with different evidence to find a value that fits your scenario.

docs.title: Combined Context Influence
docs.text:
Influence values describe each context on its own, and their probabilities are averaged. Sometimes only the combination of instantiations says something, e.g. the speech command pickup while the human is working is strong evidence for pick up tool, much stronger than the average of both.

A combined context influence sets one influence value for a combination of instantiations of two or more contexts. If all of them are observed (or assumed during inference), the combined value replaces the single influence values of these contexts. If several combinations match, the first one counts.

docs.title: Configuring Combined Context Influence
docs.text:
In Combined influences, Add opens a dialog: 1. Choose the intention. 2. Choose two or more contexts and one instantiation for each (+ Context adds another one). 3. Choose the influence value of the combination.

The list shows all combined influences, the trash icon removes one.

docs.title: Graphical Representation
docs.text:
The Graph shows the two-layer Bayesian net of your config: contexts on the left, intentions on the right.

  • Edges connect every context with every intention. The thicker and the more orange an edge, the higher the influence. For a folded context the edge shows the mean influence of its instantiations; an influence of 0 is a thin dashed line.
  • Clicking a context unfolds it into its instantiations, each with its own edges, and selects the context in the Influences table. Click it again to fold it.
  • Clicking an intention highlights its column in the Influences table, clicking an edge selects both.
  • Combined influences are the dashed boxes in the middle: dashed lines come from the combined contexts, the edge to the intention shows the combined influence value.
  • Use the buttons in the corner to zoom or to fit the graph.

The graph changes with every edit, so you can check at a glance which contexts drive which intention. The Qt configurator has a similar graph.

docs.title: Example Scenario
docs.text: Here we describe an example scenario which can be loaded from the file small_example.yml. We have a very small scenario where a human can be assisted by a robot. In this scenario the human either wants the robot to pick up a tool or hand over a tool. What the robot can perceive is if the human is holding an object, the human activity and a speech command from the human.

docs.title: 1. Context Setup:
docs.text:
• speech commands: The context speech commands has the following three instantiations: pickup, hand over, other
  • human holding object: The context Human Holding Object can either be True or False
  • human activity: The context human activity can either be working or idle

docs.title: 2. Intention Setup:
docs.text: In this scenario we only have the intentions hand over tool and pick up tool.

docs.title: 3. Setting Values:
docs.text:
• Apriori Probabilities for Context
  • To set the apriori probabilities for the context instantiations, we have to ask ourselves "How likely is it that this instantiation occurs". If we have no knowledge about that it is a good fit to just equally distribute the probability over all instantiations.
  • Influence Values for Context-Intention pairs
  • For every Context-Intention pair you need to ask yourselves "How much influence has this context instantiation on this intention".
  • Decision Threshold:
  • For our scenario we set the decision threshold to 0.8. This means that for any intention to be recognized as valid, the associated probability must exceed this threshold. With 80% we assure that the system must be quite confident for the inferred intention.
  • Cobined Context Influence
  • Most of the cases can be covered by just setting the influence values for all Context-Intention pairs. But in some cases there is the need to give a very specific influence to the combined occurrence of two or more contexts. In this example we decided to give the case where the human is working while giving the speech command pick up tool a extra high influence to make sure that in this case the robot is very certain that it needs to assist the human to pick up the tool.

docs.title: 4. Outcome:
docs.text:
Load the example in the web GUI (Load example) and open the Live inference tab. Choose pickup as speech command: pick up tool gets 77 %, which is below the threshold of 80 %. Add that the human is working and holding an object: the combined influence lifts pick up tool to 95 % and it is recognized. Try other evidence to see if your configuration describes the scenario as expected, see Live inference.

You can do the same in Python with the script small_example_from_yml.py, e.g. in an interactive Jupyter shell.

In your own code, load the config and create an inference for it:

from cobair.model import Config
from cobair.infer import Inference

inference = Inference(Config.load('my_scenario.yml'))
intention, decision_threshold, probabilities = inference.infer({
    'speech commands': 'pickup',
    'human holding object': True,
})

Contexts you don't observe can be left out, their apriori probabilities are used instead. If a context is observed as a continuous value, bind a discretization function which maps the value to one of the instantiations, e.g. inference.bind_discretization_function('human holding object', lambda distance: distance < 0.2).

This example shows how the CoBaIR can assess different contextual factors and their influence on possible intentions, thereby interpreting and acting upon human intentions in a dynamic environment.

docs.title: Web GUI
docs.text:
The web GUI is the primary GUI of CoBaIR. Install and start it with

pip install "cobair[web]"
cobair-web

cobair-web serves the GUI on http://localhost:8000 and opens it in your browser.

No Node.js is needed: the frontend is pre-built and part of the package.

option config.yml config file to open, Save writes back to it (created on save if it doesn't exist) --port 8000 port to listen on --host 127.0.0.1 host to listen on, use 0.0.0.0 to open the GUI to other machines --no-browser don't open the browser

docs.title: Configs
docs.text:
• New starts an empty config, Load YAML opens a file (or drop it on the button), Load example loads the example of the Tutorial.
  • Download YAML saves the config as a file. Save is shown when cobair-web was started with a file and writes to that file.
  • Without a file, every change is kept as a draft in your browser and restored the next time you open the GUI, nothing gets lost when you close the tab.
  • With a file, the badge unsaved changes shows that the config differs from the file, and the browser asks before you leave the page. Download YAML doesn't change that file.
  • Undo / Redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y) step through your changes. While you type in a field, the shortcuts undo the text.
  • Click the heading of a section or a context to fold it.

The config is only sent to the cobair-web process that serves the page, nothing is stored on a server.

docs.title: Editing
docs.text:
The Tutorial explains every setting; the info icons in the GUI link there.

  • Contexts: Add or the pencil icon open a dialog for the name, the instantiations and their apriori probabilities. Apriori probabilities can also be changed directly in the cards.
  • Intentions: Add, rename (pencil icon) and delete (trash icon).
  • Influences: choose a context, then choose a value for every instantiation and intention.
  • Graph: click a context to unfold it and select it in the influence table, click an intention to highlight it.
  • Combined influences: Add a value for a combination of instantiations, remove it with the trash icon.
  • Decision threshold: a number between 0 and 1.

Problems of the config (e.g. apriori probabilities that don't sum up to 1) are listed at the top while you edit.

docs.title: Live inference
docs.text:
The Live inference tab tests your config while you build it:

  • Choose for every context what is observed, or unknown. Unknown contexts use their apriori probabilities.
  • The chart shows the probability of every intention, the dashed line is the decision threshold. The intention above the threshold is highlighted and named above the chart, otherwise no intention is recognized.
  • The graph shows the observed instantiations and colors the intentions by their probability.
  • Switch back to the Editor, change values and come back: the evidence is kept and the result recomputed.

In your own code, the same inference is cobair.infer.Inference(config).infer(evidence), see the API.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
The web GUI is a Reflex app in cobair/web (Reflex is pinned to an exact version).

  • Run it with hot reload: cd cobair/web && reflex run
  • Build the frontend that is shipped in the package: python -m cobair.web.build (Reflex downloads the JavaScript tools it needs). In a source checkout (pip install -e ".[web]") cobair-web does this by itself when the sources in cobair/web changed since the last build, e.g. after switching branches; otherwise the browser would keep reloading because the frontend doesn't match the backend state.
  • Tests: pytest tests/web. The end-to-end tests start cobair-web and need the built frontend and Playwright (pip install --group e2e && playwright install chromium).
